rows.whyTheElectionIsWithdrawn: Not a bug and not an oversight. The build applies a row-integrity rule — a row is completed or left untouched — and Form A item (d) is one sworn compound sentence with nine fill-in cells. reports/actual-writes.json names the withdrawal explicitly under heldButNotPrinted, reason 'withheld_for_row_integrity': `guilty`, plus the three cells the platform DOES hold for that row (guiltyDt 2019-11-02, guiltyOff1, guiltyCrt), are all withdrawn because six sibling cells could not be printed. The guide discloses the withdrawal at '## Values this platform holds but did not print' and again at '## Where self-help ends'. So the disclosure obligation is met; the ELECTION obligation is not, and the contract is explicit that disclosing an election the route determines is not the same as making it.
rows.whyThisLaneDidNotJustTickTheBox: Because on THIS route ticking it cannot be done truthfully from anything the repository holds, and the obstacles are legal rather than mechanical. Each was verified first-hand at this base:
theObstaclesVerifiedFirstHand: THE STATUTE LINE HAS NO LAWFUL VALUE ON THIS ROUTE. Item (d) prints 'in violation of N.J.S.A. (statute(s))'. This family's track is nj_ordinance — legal-design-track-registry.json, legalName 'Expungement of Municipal Ordinance Offences (N.J.S.A. 2C:52-4)', dispositions exactly ['convicted']. A municipal ordinance offence is not an N.J.S.A. offence, so the cell the form prints has no correct entry drawn from the matter. Ticking (d) therefore either swears to a conviction whose statute line is blank, or invents a state statute into a notarized petition.

THE INCARCERATION CELL CANNOT BE ANSWERED 'NONE'. `guiltyTimeType` is a dropdown, and its /Opt list read by pdf-lib directly from the pinned source binary is exactly ['  ', 'jail time', 'prison time', 'incarceration time']. There is no 'none' and no 'fine only'. For the ordinary municipal-ordinance sentence the only non-false entry is the blank option, which is the source's own default — so ticking (d) swears to completing an incarceration term the form gives no way to decline.

TWO CELLS ARE COLLECTED BY NO QUESTION ON THIS TRACK. legal-design-intake/NJ.memo.json, track nj_ordinance, has eleven participantInputs. Read one by one against item (d): the conviction date, offence, statute and court come from ordMatterDetails; probation and release dates come from ordSentenceCompletion. But the FINAL SENTENCE IMPOSED (guiltyFinal1, guiltyFinal2) is asked by no question at all, and the DATE FINES WERE PAID (guiltyFineDt) is not either — ordFinancialAssessment asks whether every assessment is paid and why not, never when. So the row cannot be completed from intake even with a richer persona.

NO OTHER CONTROL ON THE KIT CAN STATE THIS ROUTE. All nineteen checkboxes on the pinned kit were enumerated with pdf-lib and their printed captions read. The only conviction-shaped election on Form A is `guilty` (and its continuation twin `contGuilty`). The two other route-shaped boxes name other statutes on their face — delivered page 22 prints seek5yrs as 'pursuant to N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2(a)(2) … or … 2C:52-3(b)(2)' and seek34degree as 'pursuant to N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2(c)(3)'. Nothing on the kit says 2C:52-4, and the closing prayer is the generic 'as authorized by N.J.S.A. 2C:52-1, et seq.'

THE FIXTURE PERSONA IS NOT AN ORDINANCE PERSONA. The facts held for this family describe a state crime, not a municipal ordinance matter: matter.charge is 'Possession of a controlled substance' and matter.case_number is '24-CR-001234'. Even if item (d) were completable, this persona would not produce an ordinance petition. Authoring one requires knowing what belongs on the N.J.S.A. line, which is the first question above.
rows.theStandingReleaseBlockerOnThisTrack: legal-design-intake/NJ.memo.json, track nj_ordinance, carries ONE unresolvedQuestion with impact 'release_blocker': 'The full text of N.J.S.A. 2C:52-4, including whether ordinance convictions count toward the offence caps on the indictable and disorderly persons tracks. The section was not obtained at an official New Jersey channel, and only the two-year period is confirmed, from the New Jersey Courts self-help page.' The track registry's own mechanism sentence repeats it. The route record therefore does not itself hold the statute this election would state.
theExactQuestionsThatMustBeAnsweredBefor: Q1. Form A (CN 10171) item (d) prints 'in violation of N.J.S.A. (statute(s))'. On a N.J.S.A. 2C:52-4 municipal-ordinance matter there is no N.J.S.A. offence section. How does the New Jersey Judiciary want an ordinance matter identified on that line — the municipal ordinance code and section, the words 'municipal ordinance', 2C:52-4 itself, or something else? Until this is answered the packet cannot tick item (d) without either leaving a sworn statute line blank or writing a state statute that does not describe the conviction.

Q2. `guiltyTimeType` offers only ['  ', 'jail time', 'prison time', 'incarceration time']. What does the Judiciary intend a filer whose ordinance sentence carried NO custodial term to enter, and does leaving the dropdown at its blank default while ticking (d) make the sworn paragraph incomplete or false?

Q3. Item (d) is one compound sworn sentence. Is a filer permitted to tick (d) and leave the cells the platform does not hold for the participant to complete before filing — the REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING shape the contract otherwise allows — or must the paragraph be whole before the box may be marked? This is the question on which the whole repair turns: it is the choice between the build's row-integrity rule and the contract's ROUTE_OPTION_NOT_SELECTED rule, and it is a question about a notarized New Jersey petition rather than about this build.

Q4. The standing release_blocker: obtain the full text of N.J.S.A. 2C:52-4 at an official New Jersey channel, and settle whether ordinance convictions count toward the offence caps on the indictable and disorderly persons tracks.
rows.whatWouldNotSatisfyTheObligation: Writing more guidance. The guide already discloses the withdrawal in two places and already names the ordinance/N.J.S.A. problem in its own words. VF11 addressed this directly and this lane agrees on the reading of the contract: ROUTE_OPTION_NOT_SELECTED means 'an election the route determines, left for the participant', so telling the participant to tick the box themselves is the defect restated, not the defect cured. Adding a third disclosure would move bytes in the guide, change nothing on the petition, and let a family reach terminal on a petition that still states no route.

That asymmetry is a reason to answer Q1–Q3 before spending the raster, not a reason to take the cheap branch.
